svg.title: Comparing four RP discovery methods: static, Auto-RP, BSR and Anycast-RP with MSDP
svg.desc: Four rows in a comparison table. Static RP: standard, configured by hand on every router, no protocol overhead, but every change is a network-wide edit and there is no automatic redundancy. Auto-RP: Cisco proprietary, candidate RPs announce to 224.0.1.39 and mapping agents publish to 224.0.1.40, needs sparse-dense-mode flooding. BSR: RFC 5059, candidate RPs unicast to the BSR which floods the RP set hop by hop on 224.0.0.13, standard and multi-vendor but slower and needs BSR election tuning. Anycast-RP plus MSDP: several RPs share one loopback address and synchronise source-active state over MSDP, giving load sharing and fast failover at the cost of a full MSDP mesh. Each row is rated on standardisation, control overhead, convergence and automatic redundancy. A footer states the biggest trap: when a static RP list maps different groups to different RPs, the mapping must be identical on every router, otherwise some receivers join the wrong RP and the fault looks like some people can watch and some cannot.
svg.text: Four ways to learn who the RP is, and what each one costs you later
Pick by standardisation and by failure behaviour. "It converges" is not the same as "it fails cleanly".
a change is a network-wide edit
C-RP unicast to BSR, hop by hop
The trap with several RPs: if a static RP list points different groups at different RPs, that mapping must be byte-identical on every router -
one device that maps differently produces "some receivers joined the wrong RP", which reads in the ticket as "half the people can watch".

Reading the table: there is no row that wins everywhere. Static wins on determinism, BSR on portability, Anycast on failure behaviour - and the failure behaviour is the column that gets tested at 2am.

Scale rule of thumb: one campus, one RP plus an Anycast backup. Multi-site WAN, one Anycast pair per region so registrations stay local. Large enterprise, split RPs per business domain so video and market data cannot hurt each other.
